CholeskyQR2 at n512: Ozaki Gram NS=4 (FP64-class INT8 TC) + batched FP64 chol + FP32 tri_solve_right_inv + orhr_col recon, 2 passes, good/bad gate w/ geqrf fallback. Fixed an illegal-access (S scratch must be (b,n,n) not (n,n)). 22 base test shapes PASS but diff+invariance guards FAIL on orthogonality: residual ~0.02-0.036 vs 0.0061 gate (scaled 24-584). Root cause: FP32/TF32 tri_solve loses precision for kappa(A)~1e5 dense cond2 (probe: FP64 solve->orth 1e-4, FP32 solve->orth 0.97); colnorm-only good-gate (5e-2) too loose to catch off-diagonal orth loss. Next: Newton-Schulz orth polish (TC GEMMs) or FP64 solve.

CholeskyQR2 at n512 PASSES via tau-override recon fix: override tau_i=2/(1+||v_i,below||^2) so each Householder reflector H_i=I-tau_i v v^T is EXACTLY orthogonal regardless of the FP32/TF32 recon precision; orth collapses from 3-6x gate to 0.4x gate at kappa=1e5 (the residual error lands in the 200x-slacker factor gate). VALIDATE PASS (22 tests + diff_correctness + invariance B=1280 + kernelguard). Benchmark geomean 6366.9us. Per-shape: n512 dense 52261, mixed 357161, rankdef 1114826 (0/640 good->ALL geqrf fallback, the killer), clustered 52237; non-n512 shapes unchanged. Profile (contaminated by checker) shows INT8 Ozaki Gram GEMM fine (~1.2ms), but many separate launches (Gram/chol/solve/recon/R-accum) = launch-bound. Next: replace geqrf fallback with fast exact-Householder; then fuse.

Next: cheap pre-classify to skip wasted CQR2; nb sweep; assess if fused megakernel can close 14x.

KEY DISPROOF nailed this iteration: pass-0 CANNOT avoid FP64 -- FP32 pass-0 Gram loses 35 matrices/shape to fallback, FP16/BF16+shift lose ~all (shift swamps the small singular values at kappa=1e5). So the FP64-class tax on pass 0 (Ozaki Gram 3.5ms + FP64 chol 5.8ms) is intrinsic; mixed/rankdef still waste it before bailing.

Built the first CORRECT, VALIDATING CholeskyQR2 path at n512 (best def31a67, geomean 3167us; 22 tests + diff + invariance + kernelguard all PASS). VERDICT: CQR2-at-n512 is a confirmed DEAD END vs the champion (1644us) -- the all-good case (dense/clustered) is intrinsically ~10x slower (37ms vs 3.6ms). Three airtight reasons: (1) kappa(A)~1e5 at cond=2 forces FP64-class pass-0 Gram+chol -- PROVEN unavoidable (FP32 pass-0 loses ~35 matrices/shape to fallback; FP16/BF16+shift lose ~all because the shift swamps the small singular values). (2) The fused per-matrix megakernel the brief envisioned is ARCHITECTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE at n512: one 512x512 FP32 matrix=1MB >> 228KB SMEM (only works for small n like the n176 mega). (3) chol/solve/recon are sequential/triangular, NOT GEMM-bound, so fusion can't make them FP16-fast; the champion's FP16 Householder is 10-40x cheaper per FLOP. SALVAGEABLE NUGGET (reusable anywhere orhr_col is needed): the tau-override recon fix -- override tau_i=2/(1+||v_i,below||^2) so each Householder reflector is EXACTLY orthogonal, which DEFEATS the documented 'TF32 recon caps at kappa~6000' wall (orth -> 0.4x gate independent of kappa; error lands in the 200x-slacker factor gate). Code in _cqr2_reconstruct_tau_fixed. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT re-brief CQR2-at-n512. The only live GEMM-dominant angle at n512 is making the CHAMPION's FP16 trailing GEMM faster (custom CuTe tcgen05 FP16 batched GEMM vs cuBLAS at the n512 IB-width tiles), NOT replacing Householder with CholeskyQR.
